[h1]Dear Gunsmiths,[/h1]

The moment has come! [b]The Fabryka Broni DLC[/b] is officially out! Starting today, you can dive into the world of legendary Polish firearm designs – and to celebrate the release, the DLC is available with a [b]10% discount![/b]

notes.title: THE NEW UPDATE FOR GUNSMITH SIMULATOR: ANTIQUES IS NOW AVAILABLE!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35193301/e0903ee7df1358857cf46cb3ce3d8811850b2c79.png[/img]

Dear Gunsmiths,

We’ve got some exciting news for you! We’ve just released a brand-new update for Gunsmith Simulator – Antiques! Along with it comes the premiere DLC Flint & Powder, which will let you explore the secrets of antique firearms. It’s time to dive into the fascinating world of historical treasures and unique challenges!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3288480/Gunsmith_Simulator__Flint__Powder/
https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/49261/Gunsmith__FlintPowder/

In addition, to celebrate the new update, we’ve prepared a special 36% discount on Gunsmith Simulator! It’s the perfect opportunity to join our gunsmithing community and enjoy all the new features. Take advantage of the offer before it’s gone!

[h3]What’s included in the update?[/h3]

This update introduces a division between replicas and antiques. Replicas are guns that look like the original but are entirely made of new parts, while antiques are true treasures – firearms that are at least 100 years old, made entirely of original components, and have museum-level value. Antique guns will be much more expensive but also significantly harder to repair – a real treat for collectors and history buffs!

As part of this update, we’ve also introduced a new tool – the bench grinder. This machine allows for more delicate work with metals, preserving the integrity of antique weapon components. With it, you can restore these precious artifacts without risking damage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35193301/7342766a9a0b6850fb9506a35f4ad4b2a1698388.gif[/img]

Another new feature is wood waxing. This excellent method helps preserve old wood and draws inspiration from techniques used by gunsmiths of the past. With this option, your work will gain authentic character and timeless appeal.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35193301/e33a22fba78930753c6189f2ff16eaaff79259d9.gif[/img]

We hope these new features will make your adventure with Gunsmith Simulator even more exciting. We encourage you to grab the Flint & Powder DLC and immerse yourself in the world of antique firearms!

Best regards,
The GameHunters Team

Hello again, Gunsmiths!

We’re back with another exciting update that’s sure to delight every one of you! We've just released the latest update for our game, Gunsmith Simulator! What’s new, you ask? We’ve added a new weapon, leaderboards, expanded attachments, and the ability to paint them. Check out our video to see all the new features in action!

[previewyoutube=YZmocdCM2jA;full][/previewyoutube]
Now for the details!

One of the new additions is the introduction of a new weapon model – the Ruger Precision Rifle, the first modern sniper rifle implemented in our game. This model, introduced to the market in 2015, quickly gained recognition among sport shooters and hunters for its precision and versatility. The Ruger Precision Rifle allows easy barrel replacement and the use of various magazine types, making it incredibly versatile. Now you can try out its capabilities in our game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35193301/d6faf921d7c847fdcad81df7b17dfb30bb5b5190.gif[/img]

Another new feature is the leaderboards, which are online tables that will allow you to compete with other players in mini-games. You’ll also be pleased with the expanded attachments. You can now slide attachments along rails and place them wherever you want. The exception is optics, which must be mounted on a thread or rail according to its mount. Additionally, you can now paint them just like your weapon!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35193301/2ee0bc483be6a5aea6e146024c4391610f4de579.gif[/img]

From now on, the game will also allow you to remove parts of the weapon while working on it, giving you even more freedom to modify your equipment!

Share your impressions of the latest update. We look forward to your comments and feedback on our Discord!

notes.title: New shooting ranges
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35193301/d4c68ba35207e4c0181f5c82c42a6fc1c70ddb15.png[/img]

Hello Gunsmiths!

Do you remember we created a survey a while ago asking what kind of facility you'd like to see in a shooting range? Something that in your opinion could make it more attractive? Well, that's exactly what we did... Today we'd like to officially announce that [b]CQB won most of your votes[/b]. But... that's not all! Inspired by your responses, we decided to combine it with other facilities. In total, CQB will feature [b]three new zones[/b] with short-distance shooting. In the text below, we'll describe the mechanics of the entire facility and show it in screenshots.

Ok, so let's get to the point... CQB will be located in a post-industrial brewery, where a shooting range has been set up for training. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35193301/63ee365fc2f3d43b4622a371e4fc877b6512adb6.png[/img]

As we mentioned, we've broken it down into three parts related to the short-range shooting. Here are these objects:

- [b]Killhouse[/b] - this is a building combat simulation where you have to cross the track on time and eliminate the targets, but not hit the "hostages",

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35193301/ed61262ae19f85865ecc9916f57ad81557d1bcc8.png[/img]

- [b]Indoor Shooting Range[/b] - underground is a shooting range with moving targets. You'll have to hit the group of moving targets as quickly as possible,

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35193301/ccc8b24ba0f7a455e4c22b8a26f3e3c3669282e9.png[/img]

- [b]Destruction Range[/b] - is a zone for arbitrarily smashing a variety of targets, such as fruit or a water bottle. It's also supposed to be there to compare the effects of hitting with different bullets.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35193301/e16c40d83301fbc2713a8bc46845fc1bb0462a6b.png[/img]

Let us know how you like the newest shooting ranges We're waiting for your feedback!

See you soon!

notes.title: Devlog #3
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35193301/d3d32c267056a87cdf4851f159ab9fc4d905c169.png[/img]

Hello, Gunsmiths!

First of all, [b]we would like to thank you for your presence and support[/b]. Working on the game is a very long and hard process, but your support gives us great motivation to continue!

You're probably curious what we're up to and how work on the game is progressing. That's why today we come to you with another, [b]third devlog[/b], in which we will introduce you to some of the gunsmithing works that you will meet in our workshop.

Ok, so let's start at the beginning. The basis for working with guns is to take them apart. This will allow you to assess the degree of dirt, rust and damage to the various parts of the weapon.

[b]SANDBLASTING[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35193301/daac211d7c9abbe1d6bc770cbc62aa8a3da88be0.png[/img]

If we have done this, we can move on to cleaning the weapon. We can do it with a simple rag or we can go a step further and use a more advanced option - [b]using the sandblasting process.[/b]

As you know sandblasting is a technological process which consists in cleaning or shaping a surface with an abrasive material in a stream of compressed air or liquid. This is somewhat similar to sanding, except that the cleaned surface is more even and gets the roughness required for painting and there are no problems with cleaning hard-to-reach corners or curves. It’s worth mentioning, however, that while sandblasting is a quick way to do it, it is not suitable for precision mechanism parts or antiques in general.

So let's take a look at what this process will look like in our workshop. You will be able to use sandblasting cabinet for it. Just put the parts you want in there and go. Below you will find the video of this process.

[previewyoutube=tNrw3AtuLCU;full][/previewyoutube]
[b]BLUING[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35193301/8cd9587c090509219cd94b7730a99e5b07040553.png[/img]

In addition to rust, the old oxidation is also removed, because it's rusty and is no longer even.

Ok, now a few words about [b]bluing[/b]. It’s the process of coating the surface of metals with a thin layer of their oxides. This activity is intended to provide protection against corrosion, but is also done for decoration. Now we will show you how bluing will work in our game.

We have a table with four tanks. Looking from the top, the following tanks are located here:
- Caustic Soap Tank,
- Cold Water Rinse Tank,
- Bluing Salts Tank,
- Hot Water Rinse tank.

First you have to turn on the heating. Then you must clean parts in caustic soap solution, rinse in cold water, oxidate in the bluing tank and again rinse in cold water. At the very end you have to rinse parts in hot water and voila - oxidation finished. Now you can take out blued parts.

[previewyoutube=4x_hbBk-mC8;full][/previewyoutube]
Don't worry, even if you haven't memorized the order in which you dip the parts into the tanks, it's okay. The game will tell you in which tank to place the metal gun parts.

That's more or less how it will all look in our game.

Let us know how you like it and write what your experiences are with sandblasting and bluing parts. We would love to read it!

And more news from our game coming soon!

Stay tuned!

notes.title: Gunsmiths! Check your guns!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35193301/286036b513f0bfef417a1f355953eb42a1305b37.png[/img]

Hello, Gunsmiths!

We come to you with something that you have been waiting for a long time. Some time ago, we presented you an online questionnaire, in which from among the presented weapons, you could choose the ones you would like to see in our game. This or those weapons that [b]received the most votes will be placed in Gunsmith Simulator.[/b]

Well... We have to admit that, as usual, you didn't fail and took a large part in our vote. Your commitment has exceeded our expectations, for which we thank you very much.

We would like to emphasize that the differences in the results between the various weapons were small, sometimes only two or three votes, but according to our assumption, we chose the ones that received the most of your votes.

[b]Below we present the results:[/b]
1. M4 Carbine
2. Colt M1911
3. Moseberg 590A1

We hope you enjoy the results!

We also remind you of the possibility of tracking our social media. You will find there, among others screenshots from the game that aren't on Steam. You can find all the links [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1101120/discussions/0/2787116918298357058/]HERE.[/url][/b]

Hear you soon!

notes.title: CHANGELOG - JUNE 2019
notes.content:
Howdy, fellow gunners?
Hope you good! Sorry for keeping you uninformed. Don’t worry, game isn’t fake, we are working on it. After polishing alpha version we will show you our progress. For now keep some changelog:
Couple of guns can be fully disassembled for testing purpose
Project of shooting range where you can test your crafted guns 
Available mode: shooting to zombies on shooting range :)
Market manager where you can sell crafted weapons and buy materials to make new ones
Raw design of a gunsmith workplace (where the tools should be placed, where you keep materials)
A little bit of bug fixing

What’s left to do?
A little bit of bug fixing
Animations (a lot of)
3D Models (a lot of splitting)
Gun sounds (to please gun lovers like you) 
USA, Soviet and China guns will be in game for sure
